title: Unit – 2 : Session – 5 | Harmony of the Self with the Body — Self-regulation and Health
sections: Q1. SELF-REGULATION (sanyam) is the feeling of responsibility in the Self for nurturing, protecting and rightly utilising the Body — neither neglecting it nor indulging it. HEALTH is the state of the Body being in harmony — fit to act according to the Self's instructions. RELATION: when the Self lives with the feeling of self-regulation, it gives the body proper food, rest, exercise and avoids harmful indulgence — health then follows as a NATURAL OUTCOME. Health thus indicates harmony of the Self with the Body; self-regulation is the cause, health the effect.

Q2. PROSPERITY = the feeling of having/producing MORE THAN REQUIRED physical facility. TWO STEPS: (1) Right ASSESSMENT of need — knowing, with right understanding, how much is actually required (needs are limited and identifiable); (2) COMPETENCE/ability to produce or ensure more than the assessed need. Without step 1, no amount of production creates the feeling of prosperity; without step 2, the assessment remains theoretical. Both together make prosperity a feeling grounded in reality.

Q3. Two gross misunderstandings: (1) 'HUMAN BEING = BODY' — hence happiness = sensation and respect = possessions, driving unlimited consumption; the DATA shows needs of the body are limited and temporary while needs of the Self are continuous — so body-centred living can never satisfy. (2) 'RESOURCES ARE LESS THAN NEED' — the assumption of scarcity; the DATA (production figures vs population needs) shows the world produces more than enough food/goods per person — the shortage is artificial, created by unlimited accumulation and misdistribution. Together these myths sustain competition, hoarding and exploitation.

Q4. A PROSPEROUS person feels 'I have more than required' and thinks of SHARING, nurturing others and right utilisation — facility becomes a means for relationship and contribution. A DEPRIVED person feels 'I do not have enough' and thinks of ACCUMULATING, grabbing and exploiting — irrespective of actual possession. The difference is the FEELING and its resulting intention, not the bank balance.

Q5. FAMILY PROSPERITY CHART (example — FOOD): Assessed need: balanced meals for 4 members ≈ defined monthly quantity/cost. Availability/production: family income and stores comfortably exceed this need. Feeling: we feel we have enough and can also offer food to guests/neighbours. VERDICT: in the category of food, my family is PROSPEROUS. (Doing this for each category — clothing, shelter, gadgets — shows where the feeling of sufficiency exists and where accumulation anxiety persists.)
